latest_final: The student was using HKU's online course-selection system before the deadline. He had made his course choices and believed they were set, but the selections were only in a temporary/unsaved state on the system—never actually committed as registered enrollments. When the system synchronized or the session ended that evening, the unconfirmed choices did not persist, leaving his course list empty. So from his point of view, all of his courses had been "gone in one evening": not cancelled by others, not lost to a system crash, hack, deadline, full classes, or his own intentional dropping, but because the choices were never properly saved to the server as final enrollments. When he checked, every slot was blank, and the courses he wanted appeared to have vanished in a single evening.
